inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,929 Python-split lines from title page through references. The source is a coherent article whose main chain runs from harmonic decomposition and scalar projection, through constrained-Epstein contour shifting and zeta-zero residues, to zero-annihilating functionals, Virasoro obstructions, the high-temperature Riemann-hypothesis reformulation, and exceptional c=1 and c=2 derivations. Prose and equation labels make the mathematics recoverable, although several extracted display formulas have reordered tokens and therefore retain formula/text-layer representation dependence.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata, abstract-level claim, and navigation outline; checked but not treated as depth evidence beyond routing.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates scalar-sensitive modular bootstrap, contrasts U(1)c and Virasoro settings, and states the proposed CFT reformulation of the Riemann hypothesis.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Review of harmonic analysis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Establishes the Roelcke-Selberg basis, Eisenstein analytic continuation, and the absence of scalar Fourier modes for Maass cusp forms.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1 Harmonic decomposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the square-integrable reduced U(1)c partition function and identifies constrained Epstein zeta series as scalar spectral coefficients.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Crossing equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Projects to scalars, shifts the Mellin contour across zeta-zero poles, and evaluates the remainder as an explicit arithmetic special-function kernel.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3 Functionals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs Poisson-Mellin functionals whose power action contains zeta, removes sign-indefinite zero terms, and converts the result to a derivative basis.

sections_inspected.label: 3.4 Numerical results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports scalar-gap bounds, positivity-search methodology, computational bottlenecks, and comparison with the averaged Narain scale.

sections_inspected.label: 4 General 2d CFTs
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines fake scalars for Virasoro theories, carries over the crossing equation, isolates convergence and sign obstructions, and records a conjectural scalar-only sum rule for c<7.

sections_inspected.label: 5 2d CFTs and the Riemann hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates the high-temperature subsubleading envelope to real parts of zeta zeros and supplies an SU(3)1 diagnostic with explicit finite-evidence limitations.

sections_inspected.label: 6 Future directions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Maps unresolved Virasoro-scalar and fixed-spin equations, Maass-cusp complications, and possible routes to stronger U(1)c bounds; later transfer proposals are outside the present RH scope.

sections_inspected.label: A Pole structure of scalar crossing equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses inverse Laplace transformation, discreteness, and small-gap cancellation to derive the allowed constrained-Epstein pole structure.

sections_inspected.label: B Functional action on crossing equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Evaluates Gaussian functional actions, derives odd-c closed forms, and reframes the equation through k-inversion antisymmetry for arbitrary c.

sections_inspected.label: C and C.1 c=1 reconsidered
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Handles exceptional Λ-poles, checks the free-boson crossing by theta modularity, and regularizes the apparent ζ(1) divergence in the functional.

sections_inspected.label: C.2 c=2 reconsidered
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the exceptional triple spectral decomposition, contour residues, exact c=2 scalar crossing, and its extension beyond Narain theories.

sections_inspected.label: License and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: License statement and bibliography; checked for source completion but not selected as semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Scalar projection turns modular bootstrap into a spin-sensitive RH interface
accepted_units.why_material: The passage explains why projecting to U(1)c scalar primaries is more informative than spinless energy grading and states the two distinct targets: scalar-gap bounds and a zeta-zero/RH reformulation, with a more difficult Virasoro generalization.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins at the paper's statement of its new one-dimensional crossing equation and includes the full roadmap through the announced limitations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends mainly on prose and CFT terminology; equation numbers refer back to introductory benchmark bounds but no arithmetic execution is needed.

accepted_units.title: Roelcke-Selberg decomposition separates constant, continuous, and cusp spectra
accepted_units.why_material: This is the structural harmonic-analysis basis that later lets a partition function be separated into a constant mode, Eisenstein continuum, and discrete Maass data with unique coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the upper-half-plane metric, Laplacian, square-integrability condition, eigenfunction classification, decomposition, and Petersson inner product.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on extracted formulas (2.1)-(2.5) and modular-function notation; surrounding prose preserves their roles despite display ordering.

accepted_units.title: Eisenstein analytic continuation survives scalar averaging while Maass cusp forms vanish
accepted_units.why_material: The contrast between Eisenstein constant terms and the zero scalar piece of every Maass cusp form is the reusable projection mechanism that removes sporadic cusp data from the scalar crossing equation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions, functional identities, Fourier forms, example cusp eigenvalues, and the exact x-average vanishing statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Fourier expansions (2.7) and (2.11) and the scalar integral (2.13); formula extraction is imperfect but the prose states the decisive distinction explicitly.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting an Eisenstein series makes the reduced U(1)c partition function spectrally decomposable
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring out U(1)c characters produces a primary-counting partition function, and subtracting Ec/2 cures its cusp growth so the unique harmonic decomposition can be applied without assuming the theory is Narain.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theory class, reduced partition function, square-integrability repair, full decomposition, and the c=1,2 exception notice.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses CFT character notation and the extracted display (3.3); the conceptual subtraction and decomposition are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Constrained Epstein zeta series encode the scalar spectrum and inherit a functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: The scalar dimensions are compressed into a Dirichlet series that is simultaneously an Eisenstein overlap; this dual representation supplies analytic continuation and the functional equation used in contour shifting.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes convergence, analytic continuation, functional equation, overlap identity, and the Narain lattice realization as a checked special representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on formulas (3.4)-(3.8), gamma/zeta notation, and U(1)c scalar multiplicities; lattice details are illustrative rather than required.

accepted_units.title: The shifted contour becomes an explicit arithmetic scalar crossing kernel
accepted_units.why_material: After the zeta-zero residues are isolated, the remainder is converted using the constrained-Epstein functional equation, a convergent scalar sum, and the ratio ζ(2s)/ζ(2s-1), yielding the final crossing equation with Möbius-derived coefficients and a hypergeometric kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the residue definitions needed from carried unit full_openalex_w4310081615_u02, then supplies the missing evaluation through (3.22) and its large-y consistency check.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly depends on extracted contour integrals and special-function formulas (3.13)-(3.23); prose fixes the transformation sequence and numerical/large-y checks.

accepted_units.title: Poisson-Mellin factorization forces the functional action on powers to contain ζ(s)
accepted_units.why_material: Poisson resummation makes the test sum rapidly decaying at both endpoints, so its Mellin action analytically continues as ζ(s)Mφ(s); evaluating at nontrivial zeros deletes the otherwise sign-indefinite residue terms and produces a usable sum rule.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the end of carried unit full_openalex_w4310081615_u03 to retain the definition of Φ and F, then continues through analytic continuation, zero removal, and the constrained Gaussian family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Fourier/Poisson and Mellin notation in (3.27)-(3.34); all required decay and vanishing assumptions are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Width constraints can be replaced by derivatives at the self-dual Gaussian
accepted_units.why_material: The argument identifies the only unconstrained width dependence, shows its first derivative vanishes at k=1, and obtains even-derivative sum rules whose vacuum term is the ∆→0 limit, forming the numerical basis.
accepted_units.context_note: Continues directly from the finite Gaussian family and includes the justification for equations (3.37)-(3.40), not merely the final basis statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses width k, functional actions f and vac, and extracted derivative equations; the linear-algebra logic is prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Fixed derivative order yields a scalar-gap bound with apparent quadratic large-c growth
accepted_units.why_material: The first numerical regime shows a qualitative mismatch between the scalar bound and familiar linear scales: at four derivatives the fitted leading behavior is near c²/(4π²), while the authors explicitly flag the order-of-limits caveat.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes method choice, odd-c simplification, fit, proposed analytic asymptotic, and the fixed-derivative limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on numerical fit data and figure 2; values are reported by the source and are not independently recomputed here.

accepted_units.title: Discretized positivity search requires adversarial resampling and exposes two scaling bottlenecks
accepted_units.why_material: Because the functional is not polynomial-times-positive, the calculation samples dimensions, solves a linear program, checks positivity globally, and resamples negative regions; convergence slows with c while kernel evaluation grows as c^4.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the opposite-order-of-limits motivation, constraints passed to SDPB, the manual positivity repair loop, reported derivative orders, and both obstacles.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on numerical optimization equations (3.42)-(3.43) and source-reported tables; SDPB feasibility is computational evidence, not a formal theorem.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrap scalar-gap bounds and the averaged Narain scale probe different extrema
accepted_units.why_material: The source derives the averaged Narain scalar-gap scale from the integrated average density, contrasts its near-linear growth with much larger bootstrap upper bounds, and warns that an average need not resemble the optimum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition and asymptotic of the average gap, the table/figure comparison, and the authors' interpretation of the discrepancy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the source-reported average-density formula and numerical bounds; the comparison is conceptual and does not equate average with extremal behavior.

accepted_units.title: Zero-annihilating Virasoro functionals lose both convergence and sign control
accepted_units.why_material: Two independent failures are isolated: integration weakens dimension decay from exponential to exponential-in-square-root, which can lose against Cardy growth, and character coefficients vary in sign across spin, defeating a uniformly positive functional.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts with the carried fake-scalar equation's functional sum rule, gives checked low-c versus divergent high-c behavior, traces both failures to their mechanisms, and proposes changing the functional or cusp form.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses asymptotic formulas (4.5)-(4.6), Cardy growth, and character coefficients; prose explicitly records the convergence threshold behavior and sign failure.

accepted_units.title: A conjectural scalar-only Virasoro sum rule works below a sharp convergence threshold
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplying by the c=1 cusp factor suggests a scalar-only rule for general Virasoro spectra; high-dimension decay implies c<1+6 min(k,k^-1), hence c<7, and numerical tests support the rule while derivation and analytic continuation remain open.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes spectrum shifts from vacuum null states, removal of the log term, asymptotic convergence analysis, empirical precision claim, weaker bounds, and the possible c≥25 implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on extracted hyperbolic-function formulas (4.7)-(4.12) and numerical evidence; the source labels the rule guessed rather than proved.

accepted_units.title: The SU(3)1 scalar spectrum turns zeta zeros into high-temperature log-oscillations
accepted_units.why_material: An explicit c=2 model shows how subtracting the leading terms and rescaling isolates oscillations whose envelope distinguishes critical-line zeros; fitting finite-temperature data recovers early known zeros, while exponential residue decay and truncation limit the test to finite height.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the model choice and scalar partition function, includes the exceptional c=2 crossing equation, figure interpretation, residue convergence, numerical recovery, and explicit statement that this is not an independent RH check.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted SU(3)1 series, c=2 formula (5.5), and finite numerical evaluation to T=300; the bounded/unbounded interpretation includes the stated possible vanishing-residue caveat.

accepted_units.title: Virasoro scalar crossing requires harmonic analysis beyond square-integrable cusp subtraction
accepted_units.why_material: The authors identify the cusp multiplication that introduced all spins and propose that a genuinely scalar Virasoro equation may require harmonic analysis accommodating exponential cusp divergence, with the c<7 guessed rule as a boundary case.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the complete first future-direction paragraph, tied explicitly to the obstruction established in section 4.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose; η-function notation identifies the specific square-integrability device being questioned.

accepted_units.title: A fixed-spin crossing equation couples target-spin data to scalar and Maass-cusp sectors
accepted_units.why_material: Keeping a nonzero Fourier spin restores Maass cusp contributions: the Eisenstein contour can still be evaluated using scalar data and the same zeta-zero poles, but sporadic cusp eigenvalues block a comparably clean analytic equation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes motivation, full spin-j decomposition, the contour-shift argument, identified poles, and the resulting mixed-sector limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent on (6.1), Fourier coefficients, Bessel functions, and Maass overlaps; prose clearly states which terms remain tractable.

accepted_units.title: Stronger scalar bounds may require intersecting crossing systems or retaining zero residues
accepted_units.why_material: The large gap between current bounds and the averaged Narain scale motivates three concrete changes: combine scalar with traditional or four-point crossing, broaden the functional family beyond Gaussians, or incorporate rather than annihilate zeta-zero residues.
accepted_units.context_note: Covers the complete better-bounds future direction and its even-c numerical gap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-level proposals grounded in the reported table; no claim that any route succeeds is made.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian action reduces every crossing term to Bessel and hypergeometric kernels
accepted_units.why_material: The appendix computes a reusable transform library for powers, exponentials, and confluent hypergeometric terms, then assembles the exact functional action subject to the two Gaussian-width constraints.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes functional definition, auxiliary transforms, closed formulas, termwise application to the crossing equation, and the constraint reminder.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly dependent on formulas (B.1)-(B.4) and special-function notation; extraction ordering risk means later use should verify equations against the rendered source.

accepted_units.title: At c=3 the infinite arithmetic kernel collapses to a closed hyperbolic expression
accepted_units.why_material: The source shows that odd central charge can make the general functional action elementary; for c=3 the divisor-weighted infinite sum is evaluated exactly, enabling faster and more transparent positivity analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the intermediate divisor sum and its exact simplification, retaining the width constraints inherited from (B.4).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends almost entirely on extracted formulas (B.5)-(B.6); the prose reliably states the existence and purpose of the closed form.

accepted_units.title: Odd c≥5 admits a finite auxiliary-function kernel after exact divisor resummation
accepted_units.why_material: Auxiliary finite sums convert the general special-function action into an odd-c closed form, and the remaining arithmetic sum can also be evaluated exactly; this explains both numerical tractability and the c^4 growth noted in the main text.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions of the three auxiliary functions, pre- and post-resummation equations, identification of vac and f, and verification of the derivative property.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-dependent on (B.7)-(B.10) with text-layer ordering risk; reuse requires rendered-equation verification rather than trusting token order alone.

accepted_units.title: k↔k^-1 antisymmetry yields an equivalent scalar crossing equation for every c
accepted_units.why_material: Applying k^(3/2)∂k reveals an inversion-antisymmetric form that converges for arbitrary c, not merely odd c, and shows the vacuum term is the ∆→0 member of the same kernel family.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition and Bessel representation of h, all-c convergence statement, equivalent crossing equation, relation to the derivative basis, and vacuum limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (B.11)-(B.13) and Bessel notation; the inversion structure is stated explicitly in prose.

accepted_units.title: At c=1 the spectral decomposition loses cusp forms and crossing reduces to theta modularity
accepted_units.why_material: Exceptional poles change the generic decomposition: the radius-parametrized free boson has no Maass sector, its scalar spectrum makes all zeta-zero residues vanish, and the resulting arithmetic identity is checked by a Möbius divisor identity and Jacobi-theta modular transformation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the reason c=1,2 are exceptional, completed Eisenstein notation, c=1 decomposition, scalar equation, spectrum substitution, divisor resummation, and theta check.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (C.1)-(C.7), momentum/winding spectrum, and theta modularity; several displays require rendered-source verification.

accepted_units.title: A Mellin zero cancels the apparent ζ(1) divergence in the general c=1 functional
accepted_units.why_material: For a general U(1) c=1 theory the zero-residue simplification cannot be assumed. The same functional seems to hit ζ(1), but Mφ(1)=0 cancels the pole; after removing a formally divergent constant the arithmetic sum is exactly evaluated into convergent even-derivative rules.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the need to retain δ terms, includes the differentiated crossing equation, cancellation mechanism, regularized and resummed sum rules, and equivalence with the all-c inversion formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly dependent on equations (C.8)-(C.15), hyperbolic functions, and a formal-to-convergent rearrangement explicitly justified by the Gaussian constraints.

accepted_units.title: The c=2 Narain partition function factorizes into three completed Eisenstein factors plus triple cusp products
accepted_units.why_material: Repackaging the four moduli as two upper-half-plane variables exposes a special spectral factorization with a regularized Eisenstein constant and parity-matched triple Maass products, explaining why c=2 needs a separate contour analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes moduli coordinates, T-duality action, full decomposition, and the regularized E-hat definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted decomposition (C.17), modular variables ρ and σ, and regularized Eisenstein expansion (C.18).

accepted_units.title: At c=2 a pole at s=1 and zeta-zero poles produce logarithmic leading behavior
accepted_units.why_material: Scalar projection removes the triple cusp products; shifting the special contour crosses s=1 and (1+z)/2 poles, producing a log(y)/y leading term, explicit zeta-zero residues, and a convergent hypergeometric remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes scalar extraction, contour symmetry, pole classification, residue equation, exact remainder evaluation, and convergence of the zero sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent on (C.19)-(C.21), regularized Eisenstein products, and contour residues; the prose fixes pole locations and convergence.

accepted_units.title: The c=2 mechanism extends from Narain models to any gapped U(1)2 CFT
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies the minimal ingredients that survive beyond the explicit moduli factorization: subtract the regularized Eisenstein series, use the scalar gap to constrain allowed poles, and evaluate the same nonperturbative correction kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the complete final mathematical paragraph and equation, separating the general U(1)2 claim from the preceding Narain derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the compact formula (C.22) and the appendix-A pole argument; theory-dependent coefficients remain abstract.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The carried span stops after identifying and writing the contour residues; the following lines transform the remaining contour into a convergent scalar/arithmetic sum and reach the final crossing equation (3.22), so they are needed to make the advertised crossing mechanism complete.

The carried span defines the functional but stops before proving Fφ[t^s]=ζ(s)Mφ(s), applying it at nontrivial zeros, and imposing the Gaussian constraints that yield the positive sum rule; this continuation supplies the actual annihilation argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Scalar projection exposes arithmetic spectral poles
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Averaging over the modular real part kills Maass cusp modes, while the surviving Eisenstein overlap is a scalar Dirichlet series whose analytic continuation has zeta-controlled poles; contour shifting therefore converts modular invariance into a scalar crossing equation with explicit arithmetic residues and kernel.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This chain uses square-integrability after subtraction and a discrete scalar gap; it explains the appearance of zeta zeros but does not establish their real parts.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero annihilation trades sign control for weaker spectral localization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Poisson-Mellin functional deletes every zero-dependent power because its action factors through ζ(s), but the required integration weakens exponential decay in dimension to exponential decay in its square root, creating the Virasoro convergence barrier.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The obstruction is for the documented functional family; the source explicitly leaves open a different annihilator that preserves faster decay.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Empirical checks probe different links of the construction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Positivity-based scalar-gap bounds test the zero-annihilated sum rule, whereas high-temperature SU(3)1 oscillations test the retained zero residues; agreement in these channels supports different transformations of the same crossing equation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The gap bounds are solver- and discretization-conditioned, and finite-temperature recovery only reproduces already known low zeros rather than independently testing RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Virasoro extension has three separable bottlenecks
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Generic Virasoro use is blocked separately by exponential cusp growth before projection, inadequate post-functional decay, and spin-dependent sign or Maass-cusp data; the empirical c<7 scalar rule and fixed-spin equation each bypass only part of this map.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The scalar-only rule is numerically observed rather than derived, and neither analytic continuation to high c nor control of Maass data is supplied.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Inversion antisymmetry separates analytic validity from closed-form convenience
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gaussian transforms exist for general c, odd c permits exact arithmetic simplification, and k↔k^-1 antisymmetrization produces an equivalent equation for every c; closed forms improve computation but are not the source of the crossing identity's validity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: All-c convergence of the kernel does not by itself provide positivity, efficient derivatives, or sharp numerical bounds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exceptional central charges preserve the architecture after pole-specific repairs
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At c=1 and c=2 extra Λ/Eisenstein poles alter subtraction terms and leading asymptotics, but scalar projection, contour residues at transformed zeta zeros, arithmetic remainder evaluation, and zero-annihilating functionals survive after explicit regularization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The free-boson and Narain decompositions are special checks; extension to arbitrary U(1)c theories retains abstract theory-dependent coefficients and assumes the stated gap/pole control.

within_source_saturation: Saturated at the source level: every usable mathematical section and appendix was inspected, all five v1 mechanisms were carried without rewriting, and additive units cover the distinct definitions, transformations, checks, obstructions, exceptional cases, and computational logic. Further cuts would predominantly isolate display-algebra steps already represented, repeat main-text claims in appendices, or select speculative transfers outside the RH scope.
stop_reason: The article-specific mechanism chain is fully accounted for from harmonic scalar projection through zeta-zero contour residues, annihilating functionals, Virasoro failure modes, the RH asymptotic diagnostic, and c=1/c=2 pole repairs; the only unselected tail is acknowledgments, licensing, references, routine page matter, or explicitly marked out-of-scope transfer speculation, so no further non-redundant source-grounded unit remains.
